gloss: to speak up; to voice an objection; to have something to say

definitions.gloss: to speak up; to voice an objection; to have something to say
definitions.explanation: To express a complaint, objection, or opinion, especially toward someone in a position of authority or power. Carries an assertive, sometimes confrontational tone.

examples.japanese: {政治|せいじ}に{物申|ものもう}す。
examples.english: I have something to say about politics.

examples.japanese: {権力|けんりょく}に{物申|ものもう}す{勇気|ゆうき}がある{人|ひと}は{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: Few people have the courage to speak up against those in power.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{会社|かいしゃ}の{方針|ほうしん}に{堂々|どうどう}と{物申|ものもう}して、{社内|しゃない}の{改革|かいかく}を{進|すす}めた。
examples.english: She boldly spoke up against the company's policies and pushed through internal reforms.

notes:
A somewhat formal or literary expression combining {物|もの} (thing, matter) with {申|もう}す (the humble form of {言|い}う, to say). Despite containing the humble verb {申|もう}す, the expression as a whole conveys assertiveness — speaking truth to power. It has a slightly archaic flavor that adds weight and dignity to the act of speaking out.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {権力|けんりょく}に{物申|ものもう}す: to speak up against authority
- {社会|しゃかい}に{物申|ものもう}す: to speak out about society
- {政治|せいじ}に{物申|ものもう}す: to speak out about politics
- {物申|ものもう}す{姿勢|しせい}: an attitude of speaking up

USAGE:
Often used in headlines, opinion columns, and social commentary. The pattern 「〜に{物申|ものもう}す」 is especially common as a title format for essays or speeches criticizing something.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {異議|いぎ}を{唱|とな}える: to raise an objection — more formal and procedural
- {抗議|こうぎ}する: to protest — stronger, implies organized opposition
- {意見|いけん}する: to give one's opinion — more neutral, less confrontational
